note.explanation: Ionic compounds have strong attractions between oppositely charged ions. Covalent substances have different properties because their particles and the forces between them are different.
examples: Molten or aqueous ionic compounds conduct electricity because their ions can move.
Graphite conducts electricity because it has mobile electrons between its layers.
note.checkAnswer: Ions are free to move in the molten state and in aqueous solution.
note.simple: Think of solid ionic compounds as charged particles locked in place. When the solid melts or dissolves in water, the ions can move and carry electricity.
note.checkQuestion: Why does molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?
note.title: How bonding affects properties
steps: Identify whether the substance is ionic or covalent.
For an ionic substance, consider whether its ions are fixed in a solid or free to move.
For a covalent substance, consider the forces between molecules or the structure of the solid.
note.answer: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water because their ions can move; solid ionic compounds do not conduct.

options: The ions are fixed in position.
The ions have no electrical charge.
The crystal lattice contains mobile electrons.
The ions are too small to conduct.
mcqs.stem: Why do solid ionic compounds not conduct electricity?
rationales: Correct: the ions are tightly held in the solid and cannot move to carry charge.
Incorrect: ions are charged particles; this is not why the solid fails to conduct.
Incorrect: mobile electrons are not the reason solid ionic compounds fail to conduct.
Incorrect: ion size is not the cause; the ions cannot move in the solid.

options: Ions become neutral atoms.
Ions become free to move.
The compound becomes a covalent molecule.
The ions become larger.
mcqs.stem: Why can molten ionic compounds conduct electricity?
rationales: Incorrect: melting does not make the ions neutral.
Correct: in the molten state, ions are free to move and carry charge.
Incorrect: melting does not change the compound's ionic bonding into covalent bonding.
Incorrect: an increase in ion size is not the reason for conductivity.

options: A crystal lattice
A molecular chain
A layer of mobile ions
A gas of neutral atoms
mcqs.stem: What is the orderly arrangement of oppositely charged ions in an ionic solid called?
rationales: Correct: the orderly arrangement of ions is called a crystal lattice.
Incorrect: the section identifies the arrangement as a crystal lattice, not a molecular chain.
Incorrect: ions in a solid lattice are held in place rather than forming a layer of mobile ions.
Incorrect: the lattice consists of ions, not a gas of neutral atoms.

options: The layers can slip past each other.
Its carbon atoms form isolated molecules.
It has a very high proportion of water.
Its ions move between layers.
mcqs.stem: Why can graphite be used as a lubricant?
rationales: Correct: graphite's layers are not strongly bonded, so they can slip past each other.
Incorrect: graphite is described as a layered structure made of hexagonal rings, not isolated molecules.
Incorrect: water is not the reason graphite acts as a lubricant.
Incorrect: graphite is a covalent form of carbon, not a layered ionic solid.

options: Its molecules have strong intermolecular forces.
Its molecules are ionic.
Its molecules are much larger than those of H₂S.
It has no intermolecular forces.
mcqs.stem: According to the section, why does water have a high boiling point?
rationales: Correct: the section states that strong intermolecular forces are present between water molecules.
Incorrect: water is described as a covalent molecule, not an ionic compound.
Incorrect: the stated explanation is the strong intermolecular forces, not molecular size.
Incorrect: water molecules do have intermolecular forces, and these are described as strong.

options: The water molecules surround and interact with the ions.
The ions turn into covalent molecules.
The water removes the charges from the ions.
The ions become fixed in a crystal lattice.
mcqs.stem: What happens to ions during hydration?
rationales: Correct: hydration is the process in which water molecules surround and interact with ions or molecules.
Incorrect: hydration does not turn ions into covalent molecules.
Incorrect: the section does not say that water removes the ions' charges.
Incorrect: hydration surrounds free ions in solution; it does not fix them in a lattice.

options: Diamond
Coal
Graphite
Sulphur
mcqs.stem: Which crystalline form of carbon has mobile electrons between its layers?
rationales: Incorrect: diamond has a rigid structure of carbon atoms linked by strong covalent bonds.
Incorrect: coal is described as the amorphous form of carbon.
Correct: graphite has mobile electrons between its layers and conducts electricity.
Incorrect: sulphur is not a form of carbon.

written.text: Why do lower molecular mass covalent compounds exist as gases or low boiling liquids.
written.finalAnswer: They have very weak forces of attraction between their molecules, so little energy is needed to separate the molecules.

written.text: Why HF is a liquid while HCl is a gas?
written.finalAnswer: HF is a liquid because strong intermolecular forces of attraction act between its molecules; HCl has weaker intermolecular forces and is a gas.

written.text: Why covalent compounds are generally not soluble in water?
written.finalAnswer: Covalent compounds are generally not soluble in water because water is a polar solvent and many covalent compounds do not have sufficient attraction to water molecules to dissolve.

written.text: Why does iodine exist as a solid while Cl₂ exist as a gas?
written.finalAnswer: Iodine molecules have stronger intermolecular forces than Cl₂ molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them; iodine is solid while Cl₂ is a gas at room temperature.

written.text: Compare the properties of ionic and covalent compounds.
written.finalAnswer: Ionic compounds are crystalline, brittle solids with high melting points; they conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution and are generally soluble in water. Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points, do not conduct electricity, and are soluble in organic solvents; higher molecular mass covalent compounds can be solids.

rubric.why: Gives characteristic solid structure and behaviour of ionic compounds.
rubric.description: Describes ionic compounds as crystalline and brittle.
rubric.how: Mention their crystal lattice and brittleness.

rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting points.
rubric.how: Link high melting points to strong attraction between oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: States the conditions in which ionic compounds conduct electricity.
rubric.description: Explains conduction by mobile ions in molten or aqueous ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Mention that their ions can move when molten or dissolved in water.

rubric.why: Gives a contrasting physical property of many covalent compounds.
rubric.description: States that many lower molecular mass covalent compounds have low boiling or melting points.
rubric.how: Relate low boiling points to weak forces between molecules.

rubric.why: Completes the comparison with covalent compounds' electrical and solubility properties.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds are poor conductors and are soluble in organic solvents.
rubric.how: Include both electrical conductivity and solubility in the comparison.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are crystalline solids made of oppositely charged ions arranged in a crystal lattice.
They are brittle and have high melting and boiling points because strong electrostatic forces hold the ions together.
They do not conduct electricity as solids, but conduct when molten or dissolved in water because their ions can move.
Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.

Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points when their molecular masses are low, are bad conductors of electricity and are soluble in organic solvents; higher molecular mass covalent compounds may exist as solids.

written.text: How will you explain the electrical conductivity of graphite crystals?
written.finalAnswer: Graphite has mobile electrons between its layers, which carry electrical charge; therefore, graphite conducts electricity.

examTips: This topic can appear as a short-answer or constructed-response question asking why an ionic or covalent substance has a particular property.
For conductivity questions, state whether the substance is solid, molten or aqueous, then explain whether its charged particles can move.
For melting or boiling point comparisons, earn explanation marks by naming the relevant attraction: strong electrostatic forces in ionic lattices or intermolecular forces between covalent molecules.
For graphite, include both its layered structure and its mobile electrons between the layers.
For an aqueous reaction, identify the precipitate and state that it forms from ions in solution.

explain.title: Ionic solids and their lattice
explain.body: Oppositely charged ions attract strongly and form a crystal lattice. The ions are held in fixed positions, so ionic compounds are stable solids with high melting points. If a force shifts the lattice, it can break, which is why ionic solids are brittle. Because the ions are spherical and can surround one another from all sides, ionic bonds are non-directional.

explain.title: Conductivity and hydration
explain.body: Solid ionic compounds do not conduct electricity because their ions cannot move. When molten, or dissolved in water, the ions can move and carry charge. During hydration, water molecules surround and interact with ions. In aqueous reactions, ions from different compounds can combine to form a new compound, sometimes as a precipitate.

explain.title: Covalent substances and their properties
explain.body: Many low molecular mass covalent substances have weak forces between their molecules, so they are gases or low-boiling liquids. In carbon solids, structure matters: diamond has a rigid network of strongly bonded carbon atoms, while graphite has layers that can slip past one another. Mobile electrons between graphite's layers let it conduct electricity.

explain.title: Water and molecular attractions
explain.body: The section states that liquid water has a high boiling point because strong intermolecular forces are present between its molecules. This is why the strength of attractions between molecules is important when explaining the physical states and boiling points of covalent substances.

mistakes: Saying that solid ionic compounds conduct electricity: in a solid lattice, the ions cannot move.
Forgetting that ionic compounds can conduct when molten or in aqueous solution because their ions are then free to move.
Calling the ionic lattice a molecule instead of an arrangement of ions.
Explaining graphite's conductivity only by saying it has layers; include its mobile electrons between the layers.
Confusing the strong covalent bonds within a substance with the intermolecular forces between covalent molecules.
Forgetting to identify the precipitate when describing an aqueous ionic reaction.
